chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the pre-dawn meal (suhur) for the one who intends to fast, is it obligatory upon him? So he said: There is no harm in not taking the pre-dawn meal if he wishes. And as for during the month of Ramadan, then it is preferable that he takes the pre-dawn meal; we love that it is not neglected during the month of Ramadan.
ai.seo_question: Is the pre-dawn meal (suhur) obligatory before fasting in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi distinguishes between the general legal status of suhur as recommended (mustahabb) and its elevated spiritual merit specifically within Ramadan, reflecting the Shia emphasis on maximizing acts of worship during the holy month. The Imam’s statement that 'we love that it not be left' underscores the communal and spiritual value of suhur as a means of following the Sunnah of the Prophet and distinguishing the believer's fast from that of the People of the Book.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the pre-dawn meal for the one who intends to Fast, is it Obligatory upon him?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if he does not partake the pre-dawn meal if he so desires to; and as for during the Month of Ramazan, so it is preferable that he partakes the pre-dawn meal. We<sup>asws</sup> love it that he does not neglect it during the Month of Ramazan’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Shu’ayb from abu Basir who has said the following: “

I asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about breakfast before dawn, in the case of one who likes to fast whether it is obligatory or not. The Imam replied, ‘It is fine if one likes not to have breakfast before dawn. However, in the month of Ramadan, it is better. We love not to ignore it in the month of Ramadan.”’
